title: The Poor Man and His Friend in Need
logline: A ruined man borrows 500 dinars from an old friend, opens a jewel stall, and is showered with sudden luck, until a sealed note reveals that every stroke of luck was his friend in disguise.
moral: The finest help is given so that the one helped never has to bow his head: true loyalty protects a friend's dignity as well as his purse.
tone: Warm, gently comic mystery. The audience should enjoy the windfalls with the hero, sense that something is slightly off (the blue clue, the slipped smiles), and feel the reveal as a quiet lump in the throat rather than a punchline.

beats.summary: A rich man loses everything; the room empties around him.
His wife urges him to turn to an old trusted friend.
The friend listens, then gives 500 dinars to start again.
He opens a stall in the jewel market and waits.
Three strangers arrive and ask about his father.
Market neighbours vouch that he is the dead merchant's son.
Two bags: thirty thousand dinars and jewels, his "inheritance".
A lady pays 3,000 for 500 dinars of jewels.
The doors of fortune literally swing open behind him.
He tries to repay; the friend refuses: it was a gift.
A sealed note, to be opened only at home.
The three men were the friend's relatives.
The lady was the friend's mother.
All the money and jewels came secretly from the friend.
He did it so his friend would never have to ask.
Not an inheritance but the fruit of a loyal friendship that kept his dignity.

props.description: Planned fat coin purse (drawstring pouch about 60 x 70, yellow coin mark, fill 0..1; limp and hanging when empty). The friend's 500 dinars, and the same purse coming back in S12.
Planned coin mound (n coins, glint); spills from the open bag in S8 and is stacked on the counter in S10.
Planned leather satchel (about 150 x 120 at this scale, flap, bulge 0..1, open 0..1). Two of them: the "two bags". Each has one BLUE buckle strap (the clue).

Planned cut gems in four colours (each about 26 px, hexagon with one facet line and a glint) and the small jewelBox casket with a hinged lid; also a necklace = 9 gems on a drooping curve. On the tray, in the bag, in the lady's box.

Planned small scroll used as the sealed note: rolled 90 x 26 with a red seal (seal 0..1), open 150 x 200 paper sheet with lines 0..4 of wavy writing arranged as two verse couplets (two half-lines per row with a gap in the middle).

Planned round portrait (r 46 to 70) of a person head clipped to a circle, yellow rim: the friend (S2, S17) and the late father (S6, S7, S9, S17: the man's own face at age 1 with a white beard and the yellow turban of his rich days).
The Library heart prop (catalogue props: fig, worm, heart), red, about 60 px, beside the friend medallion at the moral.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل غني قد خسر ماله كله،|وأصبح عاجزًا عن تدبير شؤون بيته.|نصحته زوجته أن يستعين بصديق قديم يعرفه ويثق به،|فذهب إليه وأخبره بما أصابه من فقر وضيق.
subtitles.en: A once-rich man lost his fortune|and could no longer support his household.|His wife urged him to ask|an old trusted friend for help.

subtitles.ar: استمع الصديق إليه، وأعطاه خمسمئة دينار ليبدأ عملًا جديدًا.|وكان الرجل قد عمل صائغًا في شبابه،|فاستأجر دكانًا في سوق الجواهر،|واشترى بعض البضاعة، وجلس ينتظر الزبائن.
subtitles.en: The friend gave him five hundred dinars.|Having worked as a jeweler in his youth,|the man rented a shop in the jewel market|and began trading again.

subtitles.ar: جاء إلى الدكان ثلاثة رجال، وسألوه عن أبيه.|أخبرهم أن والده قد مات، فسألوه إن كان ابنه فعلًا.|جمع بعض أهل السوق، فشهدوا أمامهم أن الرجل ابن ذلك التاجر المتوفى.
subtitles.en: Three men came asking about his father.|Told the father had died,|they asked witnesses from the market to confirm the jeweler was truly his son.

subtitles.ar: عندئذ سلموه حقيبتين|فيهما ثلاثون ألف دينار، وحلي وأحجار نفيسة.|قالوا إن أباه ترك هذه الأشياء عندهم أمانة قبل وفاته،|وإنهم جاءوا ليعيدوها إلى وريثه الشرعي.
subtitles.en: They handed him two bags|holding thirty thousand dinars and precious jewels,|saying his late father had entrusted the goods to them|for his heir.

subtitles.ar: وبعد قليل حضرت امرأة إلى الدكان،|واختارت جواهر كان ثمنها خمسمئة دينار، لكنها دفعت ثلاثة آلاف دينار.|تعجب الرجل من هذه الأحداث،|وشعر أن أبواب الرزق قد فتحت له فجأة.
subtitles.en: Soon a woman arrived|and bought jewels worth five hundred dinars for three thousand.|The astonished jeweler|believed fortune had unexpectedly returned.

subtitles.ar: حمل خمسمئة دينار إلى صديقه، وقال إنه يريد رد المال الذي اقترضه.|لكن الصديق رفض، وأخبره أنه قدمه هدية منذ البداية،|ثم أعطاه ورقة وطلب منه ألا يفتحها إلا في بيته.
subtitles.en: He brought five hundred dinars to repay his friend.|The friend refused, saying it had been a gift,|and handed him a sealed note to read at home.

subtitles.ar: فتح الرجل الورقة، فوجد فيها أبياتًا تكشف الحقيقة.|الثلاثة الذين جاءوا إلى السوق كانوا أقارب صديقه،|والمرأة التي اشترت الجواهر كانت أم الصديق،|أما الأموال والحلي فقد أرسلها الصديق سرًا.
subtitles.en: At home he read verses revealing the truth.|The three men were his friend’s relatives,|the buyer was his friend’s mother,|and all the money and jewels came from his friend.

subtitles.ar: كتب الصديق أنه دبّر ذلك كله|حتى يساعده من غير أن يحرجه بطلب المال أمامه.|فهم الرجل عندها أن ثروته الجديدة لم تكن ميراثًا مجهولًا،|بل ثمرة وفاء صديق حفظ كرامته.
subtitles.en: The note explained that the friend had arranged everything|to help without embarrassing him.|The new fortune was not a forgotten inheritance,|but an act of loyalty that preserved his dignity.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English translation is a condensed summary of the Arabic (P1 omits "so he went to him and told him of his poverty and hardship"; P2 omits "the friend listened", "to begin a new business" and "bought some goods and sat waiting for customers"; P3 and P4 are compressed; P7 adds "At home"); both are kept verbatim and chunked by sense as closely as the wording allows.

Hidden clue added beyond the script: every helper the friend sends wears or carries one blue item (sashes, cap, bag straps, the lady's robe), matching the friend's blue robe, and the strangers and the lady each let one small smile slip when the jeweller is not looking; default: keep, because it makes the reveal a payoff on rewatch.
The father's death is shown only as his portrait losing its colour (no grave, no body); default: keep it this gentle.

The opening shows his riches vanishing in three pops and his yellow turban turning plain in the first 3.3 s (the script only says he lost his money); default: keep as the visual for "lost his fortune".
"The doors of fortune opened" is staged literally: three street doors swing open with gold light and then ease shut again; default: keep (it is the film's one comic flourish).

The reveal and the friend's motive are played inside a large thought cloud above the note, including a grey, struck-out picture of the man having to ask for money (the embarrassment the friend spared him); default: keep.

Invented English lettering (not narration): POOF!, 500 DINARS, TINK!, JEWELS, 1 2 3, HIS SON!, THUD!, 30,000 DINARS, IN TRUST, THE HEIR, 500, 3,000!, REPAID?, A GIFT!, HIS RELATIVES!, HIS MOTHER!, HIS GIFT!, THE PLAN, THE END; default: keep all 19 (mostly numbers and three reveal labels).
The time card over "وبعد قليل" reads SOON AFTER... instead of the usual LATER...; default: SOON AFTER...
The man stays in his modest green tunic to the end (no change into rich clothes) so the last image is about dignity, not wealth; default: keep.
His wife is present in the reading scenes (P7 and P8) although the script does not mention her there; default: keep her as the listener so he has someone to react with.
implementation_notes: Timing: every cue in this plan is a start time from planning/inputs/timeline.md on the final MP3 (176.39 s). Build CUE from timing.json with w(p, n); do not retime by ear. Two words are interpolated in the timeline (P3 "قد" at 51.32, P6 "خمسمئة" at 110.14): cue on their neighbours ("مات" 51.32, "دينار" 110.40) as this plan does.

People: all nine humans are the Library person with costume presets and pal/age overrides listed in cast; no new character drawings. Give each a fixed seed for blinks and set LIFE.t = t once per frame.

Blue clue: define FRIEND_BLUE = C.blue once and pass it to kin1 pal.sash, kin2 pal.sash, kin3 pal.hc, the saddlebag strap and (by preset) the lady's robe. Do not add any other blue costume to the market scenes: neighbours are brown and yellow, the awning's blue is acceptable because it is the stall, not a person.

Mask on / mask off (guide section 9): the strangers' and the lady's smiles happen only while the man's gaze is elsewhere (S7 61.26-62.8 he looks right at the neighbours; S9 85.2 he stares at the bags; S10 99.4 her back is to him; S13 131.3 he has left). Key the man's gaze first, then place the smile inside that window.

Sets: palaceHall and marketStreet return anchors; take door, desk, stool, stalls[0] and doors[] positions from them rather than from the approximate numbers here (read from the catalogue image). The home is the merchant variant with shelves: [], desk: false, treasure: false; for 0-3.3 s draw the full variant and remove three clip regions on the cues (2.18, 2.58, 3.32).

The stall: draw the back of the stall, then the man (sit 0.5 on a stool at local x -22), then the counter front, the tray, gems and bags, then customers in front on the street. Customers never stand between the camera and his face: keep them left of x 400.
Rhyme S3 and S12: same camera, same marks; only his walk (short slowing steps vs long even steps), posture (tip 0.06 vs 0) and the purse (limp vs fat) differ.

Thought cloud (S15, S16): one thoughtCloud call 800 x 520 at (500, 400), scale 0.55, p keyed in at 139.2 and out at 163.94-164.45; the inside callback switches between six pictures (strangers, lady, bags, writing desk, plan map, grey struck-out begging) with a 0.25 s wipe (clip rect moving right to left). Keep every action inside the cloud outline and every figure at least 110 px on screen.
Counters: use the style counter for 500, 30,000 and 3,000 with comma formatting; the 30,000 spin runs 69.02-70.9 and the 3,000 lands on 98.78.

Camera: clamp to the world (1000 x 1230); faces of the seated couple in S14-S17 sit near y 700, so never frame lower than centre y 760. Apply hit shake (S5 counter, S8 THUD) inside the picture panel only.

Sound (SND master 0.6, only in the listed pauses): pop 46.4, low chime 52.5, pop 58.4, whoosh 64.3, chime 108.3, whoosh 109.1, pop 131.5, seal snap 134.5, end chime 176.4. The THUD of the bags at 66.14 is lettering and motion only (it falls on a spoken word).

Subtitles: use the subtitles array as chunks_ar.txt / chunks_en.txt (| marks); chunk times come from the Arabic word times. The English is shorter than the Arabic in P1-P3, so some English chunks sit under Arabic that says more; do not rewrite either.
End: last word ends 176.06; THE END pops at 176.5 and holds to 179.89 (end_hold 3.5).
warnings: Nine people appear in total; S7 has six on screen at once. Keep the neighbours small (s 0.97 to 1.0) at the right edge and check phone legibility with a still at 60 s.
S15 packs three reveals into 15 s inside a cloud; if figures fall under 110 px, enlarge the cloud to 860 x 560 and drop the couple lower (heads near y 760) rather than shrinking the figures.

The person figure is front-facing only: "kisses her hand" (148 s) and "arms round shoulders" (142 s) must read through tip, hand targets and proximity; check both with stills.
